manifest.name: dsh-capyreporter
manifest.description: CapyReporter — an always-on-top capybara task reporter for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI. A transparent floating pet that narrates each trajectory step in a speech bubble, tells you which project is reporting, alerts you when a task completes while you are away, and lets you upload your own pet art.

bundle.text:
# dsh-capyreporter bundle patch — mounts the persistent CapyReporter desktop-pet plugin.
# The host half is lib/index.js (exported as a Cordis plugin); the package.json
# "dsh.client" declaration makes the browser half available at /plugins/dsh-capyreporter/client.js.
- insert:
    - id: capyreporter
      name: 'dsh-capyreporter'

readme.text:
English | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

A local task reporter for DeepSeek Harness Web: a page pet, plus an optional transparent always-on-top Electron companion.

- Live **workspace + session** labels and a bounded **assistant milestone** preview: the collapsed bubble follows the assistant's latest statement instead of tool chatter. Reasoning stays hidden unless you opt in to *Report thinking*; switching it off discards live reasoning buffers, and completed previews never retain reasoning. Prompts, tool arguments and tool output are never displayed.
- Separate **completed, cancelled, failed, blocked, interrupted and output-limit** outcomes, using actual DSH `turn/end` events. Idle alone is not success.
- **Running subagents are visible while they work.** The headline names them (`⏳ 1 running · 2 subagents — <chat>`) and, while the main chat has no fresh assistant text, the collapsed detail reads `🤖 2 subagents running`; the count drops as they finish and their progress milestones take over. Localized throughout.
- **Only the main chat claims a finished turn.** Delegated subagent runs never raise the green *Turn complete* tick for the parent chat: while a main chat is running the headline keeps showing it, and delegated finishes (`✅ Subagent finished`, `⚠️ Subagent failed`, `⏹ Subagent cancelled`) appear as progress milestones in the details.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-capyreporter
```

0.6.27 was re-verified against **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-alpha.1** (routes, slots, client bundle serving, and agent/session events). The only peer dependencies are `@deepseek-ai/cordis` and `react`, which DSH supplies to the plugin; no DSH package version range is pinned. Refresh after a client update; host-code updates need plugin reactivation or a DSH restart. A page refresh alone cannot replace a loaded host module.

The always-on-top pet is on by default: an install without saved preferences starts the companion right away, so the pet floats above other windows. *Use page pet* turns it off; *Retry always-on-top pet* restarts it after a failed start.
Use `DSH_PET_ELECTRON_PATH` (or `ELECTRON_PATH`) for an existing Electron executable. The plugin also checks `$DSH_HOME/electron/electron.exe` on Windows (`electron` on Linux), the user npm installation, and legacy Windows install locations. No binary is downloaded automatically. macOS should use an explicit executable path.

The host's actual port is used automatically. `DSH_CAPYREP_BASE_URL` can override it with an exact loopback HTTP(S) origin, not a URL with credentials, paths or auth tokens. Remote/reverse-proxied origins are deliberately not supported by this plugin's local-only route boundary.

The page pet is hidden **only after** the companion has decoded its image, fetched activity, and reported ready. Missing Electron, a failed renderer, or a stale heartbeat keeps/restores the page fallback. Some exclusive fullscreen applications can still cover a topmost window. Empty window background is click-through; the artwork element and bubble are interactive rectangles.

| Action | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Drag the pet | Move it; dragging does not dismiss results or open DSH |
| Ctrl / Cmd + wheel over the pet | Resize, 50–250% (ordinary scrolling remains available) |
| Click, right-click, or Enter/Space on pet controls | Open controls |
| Click anywhere outside an open menu (or press Escape) | Dismiss the pet menu — in the page pet and in the always-on-top companion |
| Details / Collapse | Toggle scrollable session details |
| Go to chat | Open the session the headline refers to (running, else finished) via DSH workspace navigation; also in the pet menu. Page pet only — the always-on-top companion cannot drive the browser window |
| Pet menu → Open settings | Jump straight to the CapyReporter section of DSH settings (also in the desktop companion menu) |
| Pet menu → Enable / Retry always-on-top pet | Start the always-on-top companion, or retry it after a failed start, without leaving the page pet |
| × in the bubble's top-right corner | Close the current bubble (new activity resurfaces it); after a run ends it also acknowledges the result. The pet menu keeps *Dismiss result* |
| Drag any bubble edge/corner, arrow keys on the corner handle, or Ct

Settings → **🐾 CapyReporter** controls visibility, the always-on-top pet, size, artwork, notifications, the **Status bubble** mute duration (10/30/60/240 min, default 30), **Report thinking** (opt-in 💭 reasoning as the live milestone, off by default) and the interface **Language** (Auto plus the ten supported locales; Arabic switches to RTL and the desktop companion follows). *Auto* tracks your browser/OS language and anything unsupported falls back to English; the choice persists on the host. Artwork must be a PNG, at most **4 MiB**, with each side **1–4096 px**. SVG, arbitrary data URLs and malformed/truncated containers are rejected. Custom-to-custom changes invalidate the image revision immediately.

Image, size and toggles are saved atomically to `$DSH_HOME/capyreporter.json` (default `~/.dsh`). A legacy `homura-pet.json` is read only when that file is absent. Page position is stored separately in this browser's local storage; desktop position is session-only. Corrupt settings are logged, not silently replaced with unrelated legacy settings. Failed writes leave the previous preferences active.

**Hide pet is not uninstall.** Remove the package using DSH's plugin manager or:

Plugin HTTP handlers are separate from DSH's SPA authentication gate. This plugin rejects cross-origin/opaque browser requests, non-loopback callers/Host headers and GET mutations; it does not expose wildcard CORS. The desktop uses an activation-scoped capability held in its main process, a sandboxed renderer, restrictive CSP and an allowlisted IPC broker. See [architecture](docs/architecture.md) for boundaries, including what they do **not** protect against.

No telemetry or outbound service is used. Notifications and the always-on-top pet can expose session titles/assistant previews on your screen; disable them in shared-screen environments.

- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md)
- [Audit, comparisons and validation](docs/audit.md)
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md)

Handwritten JavaScript is the shipped source; there is no build step.

```sh
npm ci
npm test
npm run verify
npm run test:browser

Browser smoke tests use installed Chrome by default (`DSH_TEST_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chromium` for a Playwright browser) and an optional existing Electron executable. They use temporary settings and ephemeral loopback fixtures, never your installed preferences or running DSH server. Electron coverage is explicitly skipped when no binary is found. Tests and dev dependencies are not runtime requirements.
MIT. Artwork is replaceable; other projects referenced in the audit were studied for architecture, not copied into this package.
